parole.significato: a type of tripe filled with meat
parole.testo: Borrowed from Asturian banduyu (“stomach, belly”), from Latin ventriculus (“belly”). Doublet of ventrículo.
Maybe borrowed from Asturian belfu, from Latin bifidus. Doublet of inherited befo.

parole.significato: a cured meat dish, made from bits of pig meat stuffed inside a pig's cecum
parole.testo: Borrowed from Asturian botiellu, from Latin botellus. For the unexpected retention of Latin /-t-/, Coromines & Pascual propose influence from botija (“vessel”) and other such words. Cognate with Asturian botiellu, Galician botelo and Portuguese butelo.
Borrowed from Asturian fexe, ultimately from Latin fascis. Cognate with English fagot (“bundle of sticks bound together”). Doublet of fajo and haz.
Perhaps borrowed from Asturian llera, from Latin glarea.
